paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When God's word shows up, it doesn't go to the emperor, the governor or the high priests. It comes to John in the wilderness (Luke 3:2). God doesn't need the important seats to get His word out, and He never needed you to have one either.

John's message was to get ready, and real readiness shows. He tells the crowds, "Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance," and he says that having "Abraham as our father" isn't enough (Luke 3:8). Then the crowds ask, "What then should we do?" and John gives plain answers: share, collect only what you're authorized, be content with your wages (Luke 3:10-14). Repentance isn't just feeling sorry. It's a changed Tuesday morning at work, at the table and with your wallet, and you can bake that into every day.

And here's the part I LOVE. John keeps pointing away from himself to One more powerful, the One he isn't worthy to untie the sandals of (Luke 3:16). Even when telling the truth landed John in prison (Luke 3:19-20), he never stopped pointing to Jesus. So, baker, get ready, bear fruit, and keep your eyes on the One who is coming. That's how I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper!
